👮 **Wachiman** · 🟡🐛 **Consider · bug: Journal lists migrations 0000–0002 whose SQL files and snapshots are not in the tree**

This new journal lists `0000_baseline`, `0001_integrity` and `0002_account_provider_unique`. None of those `.sql` files or their `meta/000N_snapshot.json` files exist in `packages/infra-db/src/migrations/`: only the `0003` SQL and snapshot are there. The spec (`specs/2026-10-29-several-workspaces-design.md:1112-1118`) explains why: the chain belongs to PR #364, which has not merged. Until it does, `main` has a migrations folder whose journal points at missing files. `bun run db:migrate` (`drizzle-kit migrate`, `packages/infra-db/package.json:24`) would fail as soon as it tries to read `0000_baseline.sql`. The command is documented as unused today (`commands.md:33`), but it is still wired up. One option is to commit only the `0003` SQL and keep the journal out of this PR, so #364 brings the journal. Another is to land this after #364, so the folder never sits in a half-state on `main`.

<!-- wachi:finding -->

👮 **Wachiman** · 🟡❓ **Consider · question: Snapshot chain points to a snapshot that isn't on main**

This snapshot's `prevId` (`86ab3674-…`) points to a `0002` snapshot that exists only in PR #364. In this checkout, `src/migrations/` holds just `0003_cloud_asset_workspace_id.sql`, `meta/0003_snapshot.json` and `meta/_journal.json`. The journal still lists `0000_baseline`, `0001_integrity` and `0002_account_provider_unique` (`_journal.json:9-23`), but none of their SQL files or snapshots are here.

The spec explains this (`specs/2026-10-29-several-workspaces-design.md:1112-1118`), and `commands.md:32-33` says `db:migrate` and `db:generate` aren't used yet. Until #364 merges, though, main ships a migrations folder that is broken: `bun run db:migrate` would fail looking for `0000_baseline.sql`, and the chain `drizzle-kit check` validates starts from a missing parent.

Could this snapshot and the journal wait for #364, or land on top of it? Then main would carry the column only through `db:push`, which is how the spec says it ships today. If both PRs are definitely merging together, please confirm that this snapshot was generated from #364's exact `0002` snapshot. If #364's snapshot changes before it merges, the `prevId` here will no longer match.

<!-- wachi:finding -->

👮 **Wachiman** · 🟡🐛 **Consider · bug: The queue is not tied to an account, so a sign-in as someone else silently drops the owed assignments**

`QueuedAssignment` (lines 15-21) stores no `userId`, and `runOnce` sends every due entry with whichever account is signed in when it runs (`this.deps.account()`, line 116). Say user A moves items while offline, then signs out and user B signs in. A's entries go out with B's token. The server's `setWorkspace` is scoped to the owner, so it answers NOT_FOUND, and line 126 deletes the entry for good. A's cloud copies never learn their new workspace. `onConfirmed`/`setCachedWorkspace` in `library/index.ts:145` also writes to the current account's cache, not the account the entry was queued for. A fix: store `userId` on each entry and only send (and confirm) entries whose `userId` matches the signed-in account.

<!-- wachi:finding -->

👮 **Wachiman** · 🟡🐛 **Consider · bug: Synced workspaces stop sweeping `.kaipu/tmp/`, and non-synced ones never sweep their scratch folder**

`deps.stagingDir ?? join(deps.vaultDir, STAGING_DIR)` replaces the folder-local staging directory instead of adding to it. The caller (`main/index.ts:763-767`) passes `stagingDir` only when `syncedStagingFor(vaultDir)` says the folder is synced right now. That leaves two gaps:
- A folder that held a take in `.kaipu/tmp/` before it was moved into Drive or iCloud is never swept again while it stays synced.
- Detection can come back null, for example when the xattr-only check in `detectSync` times out after 2 s (`synced-folder.ts:86-91`). On that launch, takes staged in `workspace-scratch/<id>/tmp` are not swept, so recovery depends on the next detection succeeding.

Nothing is deleted, but stranded recordings stay hidden. You could sweep both directories when they exist: the scratch one with `placeByRename`, and `.kaipu/tmp/` too. Also consider sweeping a workspace's scratch folder whenever it exists, not only when the folder is detected as synced.

<!-- wachi:finding -->

👮 **Wachiman** · 🟡🐛 **Consider · bug: The main process does not check for evicted source media before hashing or copying it**

When either side is synced, `linkable` is false, so the move reads the whole source media: `fs.sha256(media)` here unless a cached hash exists, then `copyExclusive`. The only guard against an evicted (dataless) source is in the renderer (`move-flow.ts:21`, `notMovableReason` → "evicted"), and that relies on the item list being fresh. `moveItems` (`workspaces/index.ts:248-255`) accepts any `{id, assetId}` from the renderer, and nothing on this path calls `probeDataless`. If the provider offloads the file after the list was built, the move downloads it. That breaks decision 15 ("never reads an evicted file"), and a stuck provider would block this read while the move holds the workspace gate and the switch lock. A `probeDataless` check on the source media when `source.scratch` is set could refuse with an "evicted" reason before any read.

<!-- wachi:finding -->

👮 **Wachiman** · 🟡🧹 **Consider · cleanup: Comment in the "is not synced" list describes a case that is synced**

This comment sits as the last item of the `it.each` that checks paths are **not** synced. But it describes the provider root, which `syncProviderOfPath` reports as synced (`synced-folder.ts:31-34`). The separate test at line 32 checks exactly that. A reader could take it for a missing or disabled case in the not-synced table. Move it to the test at line 32 or delete it.

<!-- wachi:finding -->

👮 **Wachiman** · 🟡🧪 **Consider · tests: "answers with the path rule before detection" can't tell the path rule from a plain null**

The test uses `/Users/x/Documents/K`, and `syncProviderOfPath` returns null for that path. So the `toBeNull()` before `refresh` would also pass if `SyncStates.of` always returned null for an entry it hasn't detected yet. The path-rule fallback at `sync-state.ts:27` isn't actually exercised. The same holds for the relocation test at line 13: its new path, `/Volumes/T7/K`, is also null by the path rule. Using a `~/Library/CloudStorage/GoogleDrive-…` path, with `home` matching it, before detection would pin the fallback.

<!-- wachi:finding -->

👮 **Wachiman** · 🟠🐛 **Fix · bug: A rejected cloudState() leaves the section on "Loading…" forever**

`load` awaits `window.electronAPI.workspaces.cloudState()` with no catch, and both callers discard the promise with `void load()` (lines 33 and 35). If the IPC call rejects, the error goes unhandled, `state` stays `null`, and the section shows the `aria-busy` "Loading…" placeholder for as long as the page is open.

This does happen. `library-ipc.maintenance.test.ts:67` lists `IPC_CHANNELS.workspacesCloudState` among the channels that maintenance mode refuses, so the handler in `main/library/index.ts:187` throws there. It also throws if `cache.read` fails.

Fix: catch the error in `load` and store an error state, then render a short message such as `t("failed")`, which `assign` already uses. A later `onLibraryChanged` or epoch change can then retry.

<!-- wachi:finding -->

👮 **Wachiman** · 🟡🐛 **Consider · bug: Out-of-order cloudState responses can show the previous workspace**

`load` runs on every `workspaces?.epoch` change and on every `onLibraryChanged` broadcast. Whichever response arrives last wins, even if it is the older request. Suppose the user switches workspace while a request is still pending. If the old request resolves after the new one, the section shows the previous workspace's location, filter and unassigned list under the new workspace's name. That name comes from `workspaces.active`, so the mismatch would not be obvious.

One fix: keep a request counter in a ref, or a `cancelled` flag in the effect cleanup, and drop responses from older requests. Another: ignore a response whose `workspaceId` differs from `workspaces?.active?.id`.

<!-- wachi:finding -->

Declined, on purpose. Leaving the journal out is the riskier option. A migration file with its snapshot but no journal entry is silent: `drizzle-kit generate` (and #364's `db:check`) would treat `0003_snapshot.json` as the latest state and report no drift, while `db:migrate` would never apply `0003`. With the four-entry journal, each mismatch is loud. On `main` before #364, `db:migrate` fails at once on the missing `0000_baseline.sql` (and `commands.md` says not to use it yet). When both have merged, git reports an add/add conflict on `_journal.json`, resolved by taking the four-entry version. This PR is the top of a four-level stack, so in practice #364 lands first. The PR body and the spec (Cloud: server and client, "Migration file") record the merge rule.

Confirmed: `0003_snapshot.json` was generated by `drizzle-kit generate` from a copy of #364's `packages/infra-db` at its current head, `0002_snapshot.json` included, plus only the one column. So `prevId` is that snapshot's id. If #364 regenerates `0002` before it merges, `0003` has to be regenerated on top of it. Holding the snapshot and journal back is declined, for the reason in the journal thread: a snapshot or SQL file without its journal entry makes `db:check` pass while `db:migrate` skips the column. The column still ships with `db:push` until #364 lands, as the spec says.

Fixed in a47dea62. Each queued entry now records the account signed in when it was queued. `runOnce` sends only the signed-in account's entries (an entry queued while nobody was signed in goes with the next account). `pending(userId)` overlays only that account's catalog, and `onConfirmed` gets the userId, so the confirmation updates that account's cache. The new test queues as user A, processes as user B (nothing is sent, no overlay), then processes as A again (sent with A's token, confirmed).

Fixed in a47dea62. The sweep option is now additive: `extraStagingDirs` is swept as well as `.kaipu/tmp/`. `main/index.ts` passes the workspace's scratch folder for every registered workspace (`scratchStagingFor`), whatever this launch's detection says, and uses `placeByRename` whenever the folder is synced. New test: a part left in `.kaipu/tmp/` of a folder that has since become synced is recovered, with no hard link.

Fixed in a47dea62. `MoverFs` gains `evicted(paths)` (default `probeDataless`). When the source is synced, the mover checks the media and the webcam track before the hash or the copy reads them. Either one evicted refuses with a new `evicted` reason ("it's in the cloud: download it first", en/es). The new test checks that nothing is read, nothing is written to the target, and the source keeps its 8 files.
Fixed in a47dea62: the stray comment is gone; the provider-root case keeps its own test.

Fixed in a47dea62. `SyncStates` now takes the home folder, and the tests use a `~/Library/CloudStorage/GoogleDrive-…` path that is synced by the path rule before any detection. The relocation test detects a plain folder, then asks for the entry at a Drive path: the path rule must answer `google-drive`, so an `of()` that always returned null would fail it.

Fixed in a47dea62. `load` catches the error and the section shows "Kaipu couldn't read this workspace's cloud items. It tries again when the Library changes." (role=alert, en/es) in place of the loading state. The next `onLibraryChanged` or switch retries. New test: a rejected `cloudState` shows the alert.

Fixed in a47dea62. A request counter in a ref: only the latest request may set the state or the error. The new test holds the first request, answers a second one triggered by a library broadcast, then resolves the first with another workspace's location: the section keeps the latest answer. I checked that the test fails with the guard removed.

👮 **Wachiman** · 🟡🐛 **Consider · bug: Scratch parts swept on a launch where detection missed are placed with link(), possibly into a synced folder**

The sweep now reads the scratch folder whatever detection says (line 765), and the comment in `stranded-recordings.ts:26-28` names the case it is for: a launch where detection did not answer. But `placeByRename` still comes from `syncedStagingFor(vaultDir) !== null`. On that same launch it is false, so `placeTake` (`recording-writer.ts:113`) uses `placeNew`, which hard-links the scratch part into the workspace folder. A Google Drive folder outside `~/Library/CloudStorage` is recognised only by its xattr, and the path rule in `SyncStates.of` (`sync-state.ts:29`) misses it. If that xattr probe times out, the newly swept scratch take is linked into Drive, which is the hazard decision 15 and NIW2-577 forbid. A part in the scratch folder only exists because the workspace was synced when it was recorded, so you could always place parts from `extraStagingDirs` by rename. `placeByRename` already copies on EXDEV (`safe-place.ts:320-321`), so this is also safe for a vault on another volume.

<!-- wachi:finding -->

👮 **Wachiman** · 🟡🐛 **Consider · bug: A failed read after a workspace switch keeps showing the previous workspace's state**

`loadFailed` only renders while `state` is null (line 80). After a switch, `workspaces.epoch` changes and `load` runs again. If that read fails (for example, maintenance refuses `workspacesCloudState`), `setLoadFailed(true)` has no visible effect. The section keeps the previous workspace's location, filter and unassigned list under the new workspace's name (`active` comes from `workspaces.active`, line 51), which is the mismatch the request counter was added to prevent. You could clear `state` on failure (`setState(null)` next to `setLoadFailed(true)`), or clear it when the epoch changes.

<!-- wachi:finding -->

👮 **Wachiman** · **Looks addressed** at `a47dea6`: Addressed. Each entry now stores `userId`. `process` skips entries that belong to another account (line 138), `onConfirmed` writes to the account that sent the entry, and `pending(userId)` only overlays that account's entries plus entries queued while signed out. A new test covers the case where account B signs in after account A queued entries.

<!-- wachi:reply -->

👮 **Wachiman** · **Looks addressed** at `a47dea6`: Addressed. The sweep now always reads `.kaipu/tmp/`, plus the workspace's scratch folder whenever a workspace is registered at that path (`scratchStagingFor`). A test covers a folder that became synced. One leftover about `placeByRename` on a launch where detection missed is filed separately on `index.ts:770`.

** Major** · **Stability & Availability** · **Heavy lift** **Bound the total eviction probe for a Library listing.** If a synced provider stalls, `list()` waits for every batch before it can return any items. The probe processes 200 paths per batch in sequence, and each stat call can take five seconds. A workspace with 1,000 media files supplies about 2,000 paths, so stat timeouts alone can delay the Library by 50 seconds. Add a deadline for the whole listing probe and surface a timeout instead of waiting for every batch. ([raw.githubusercontent.com](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/niway-dev/kaipu-record/443a9b0472cffe23d503c34e1cbbfba2d80a243b/apps/kaipu-record/src/main/library/dataless.ts))

When the total deadline expires, surface a timeout instead of waiting for remaining batches; preserve the existing probe behavior when it completes in time. After applying the fix, consider running `coderabbit review --agent` for local review. Visit https://docs.coderabbit.ai/cli?utm_source=ghpr ```

Fixed in 77d67e59. As you suggest, a take found in an `extraStagingDirs` folder is always placed by rename, whatever `placeByRename` says: a part there exists only because its workspace was synced when it was recorded. `placeByRename` already copies on EXDEV. New test: a scratch take swept with `placeByRename: false` is recovered with zero `link()` calls.

Fixed in 77d67e59. A failed read now clears `state` as well as setting the error, so after a switch the section shows the alert instead of the previous workspace's location, filter and list. New test: a good read, then a broadcast whose read fails. The alert shows and the location row is gone.

Fixed in 77d67e59. `datalessPaths` takes a deadline for the whole probe (`PROBE_DEADLINE_MS`, 10 s, checked before each batch). Once it passes, every path not yet answered is reported **evicted** and no further batch is sent, with a warning in the log. Of the two possible answers I chose the safe one: an item that is in fact local only draws a placeholder for that listing, while the other answer could hand out a URL that downloads a file. A 450-path test whose batches each take 6 s stops after two batches and marks the last 50 evicted. In the spike, `stat` on Drive answered in milliseconds, so the deadline is for a stalled provider only.

Fixed in 77d67e59. `EvictionCache` no longer remembers a "local" answer: every read is authorized by a probe made for it. To keep a grid of thumbnails cheap, requests within a 15 ms window share one batched `stat` call. Only an "evicted" answer is remembered (2 s), since refusing reads nothing, and `forget()` drops it. New tests: a local answer is not reused; a file evicted right after a local answer is refused on the next read; three requests in one window make one probe.

@csdev19 The reported change addresses this finding. Fresh probes avoid reuse of a cached “local” result, while batching limits probe cost. Caching only “evicted” results does not authorize a read. The reported tests cover the original failure case. Review thread resolved. You are interacting with an AI system.

`@csdev19` The conservative fallback is appropriate. Reporting unanswered paths as evicted prevents the listing from issuing URLs that could trigger downloads. 👮 **Wachiman** · 🟡📝 **Consider · docs: The deadline is checked only between batches, so a probe can run past 10 s**

`now() >= deadline` is checked only before a batch starts (line 79). A batch that starts at 9.9 s can still take `STAT_TIMEOUT_MS` (5 s, line 19). If `stat` is killed by that timeout and prints nothing, the `lstat` fallback (lines 94-97) then runs over up to 200 paths with no time limit, and that is exactly the stalled-provider case. So the real bound is about deadline + 5 s, plus whatever the fallback takes.

Two places promise a hard bound: line 59 ("The longest a whole probe may take") and the spec (`2026-10-29-several-workspaces-design.md:1328-1329`, "bounded at 10 s for the whole listing"). Either reword both to say the deadline is checked per batch (worst case about 15 s), or check `now()` inside the fallback loop and treat the paths left over as evicted.

👮 **Wachiman** · 🟡🧪 **Consider · tests: `now = 5_000` comes after the last call, so the TTL expiry is never tested**

The test name says an evicted answer is remembered "for the window", and it does check that the answer is reused inside the window. But `now = 5_000` runs after the last `isEvicted` call, so the clock change does nothing. Nothing checks that an evicted answer older than `ttlMs` gets probed again (`dataless.ts:127`). Move the clock change before another `isEvicted("/x")` call, without calling `forget()` first, and expect the probe count to go up. As written, the line looks like a check but tests nothing.

👮 **Wachiman** · 🟠🐛 **Fix · bug: Change folder… never re-reads the workspace's folder settings file (confidence medium)**

`WorkspaceSettings` caches each workspace's folder read by id (`reads`, `workspace-settings.ts:103-106`). That cache is refreshed by `refresh(id)` (`workspace-settings.ts:145-162`). Both sibling paths that point a workspace at a folder call it: `addWorkspace` does (line 597, "An adopted folder may bring its own settings file: read it now"), and `runSwitch` does inside `persistActive` before the commit (line 547).

`relocateFolder` never calls `workspaceSettings.refresh`. After a relocate, the cache still holds the read from the old path. The usual reason for a relocate is that the old folder went missing, so that read is typically `unreadable`, and the folder's overrides stay inactive. For the active workspace, `afterCommit` even runs `notifyOverridesChanged()` (line 526) with those stale overrides. Nothing corrects this until the next capture start (`refreshActiveWorkspaceSettings`, line 167) or a switch. Until then the Settings scope view and the effective settings silently ignore the relocated folder's `settings` file, or don't show it as pending.

Suggested fix: refresh the settings before the commit, the same way `persistActive` does. For example, wrap the registry's `relocate` in `deps` so that a successful relocate runs `await workspaceSettings?.refresh(id)` (and the sync detection, see the other finding) before `relocateActive` calls `afterCommit`.

👮 **Wachiman** · 🟠🐛 **Fix · bug: Active relocate commits and re-lists the Library before the new folder's sync provider is detected (confidence medium)**

For the active workspace, `relocateActive` calls `afterCommit` inside `relocateWorkspace` (`switch-transaction.ts:135-136`). That fires `host?.broadcastLibraryChanged()` (line 529) and `broadcastState()`. `syncStates.refresh(current)` only runs afterwards, at line 755.

Until that refresh, `SyncStates.of` sees a changed path and falls back to the path rule alone (`sync-state.ts:26-30`). A Google Drive folder that is recognised only by its xattr therefore reads as not synced. In that window:
- The re-list builds `LibraryVault` with no eviction probe (`activeEvictionProbe()`, line 368, used at `library/index.ts:74`). Evicted items come back as local, with no "In the cloud" state. The renderer keeps that list until the next `library:changed`.
- `syncedStagingFor` (line 393) returns null, so a take started then stages in `.kaipu/tmp/` inside the synced folder.

`runSwitch` avoids this ordering by doing its reads in `persistActive`, before the commit. Here, run the detection (and the settings refresh) inside the `apply` step, after `registry.relocate` succeeds and before `afterCommit`. For a non-active workspace the current order is harmless.
